Self-issue Alpine Lakes Wilderness permits (free, required May 15–Oct 31) are at the trailhead register; there's a vault toilet but no potable water. From the trailhead, follow the Middle Fork Trail (#1003), which becomes the Dutch Miller …

name: Goatshead Spire
approach: Identical to the Lemah Glacier approach, which is the only documented way into this cirque. From I-90 exit 80 (Roslyn / Salmon la Sac) go north on Bullfrog Road 2.8 miles through two roundabouts, continue on WA-903 past Cle Elum Lake (about 16.8 miles total from the freeway), turn west on FR-46 and follow it roughly 4.7-5 miles, then turn right on FR-4616 for 1-1.5 miles to the Pete Lake trailhead at about 2,800 ft (47.4350, -121.1855). Follow the Pete Lake Trail #1323 along the Cooper River about 4.5 miles to Pete Lake, continue past the lake and pick up the PCT southbound for roughly 4 more miles to the Lemah Creek crossing, then follow the PCT south under a mile to where a faint, unmaintained climbers' trail leaves on the north side of Lemah Creek (marked by occasional flagging; expect deadfall/…

name: West Route
approach: From the Salmon La Sac Trailhead (end of Salmon La Sac Rd/FR-4330, ~19 mi north of Cle Elum), pick up the Waptus River Trail #1310 heading east into the Alpine Lakes Wilderness. The first mile or so rolls over a couple of low forested hills before the trail settles into a long, gentle grade alongside the Waptus River, crossing numerous small feeder creeks (reliable water the whole way) and skirting boggy meadow sections and old burn patches. Around mile 7-8 stay on the Waptus River Trail (rather than forking north toward Spade Lake) and continue to the Waptus River crossing below Waptus Lake —…
firstResearcherNote: Unsure whether the route leaves the Waptus trail before or after Waptus Lake; placed as on the way.

name: Park Glacier Headwall
approach: Southeast via Chain Lakes Trail to Ptarmigan Ridge. From Artist Point parking, take Chain Lakes Trail (682) to Ptarmigan Ridge Trail (682.1) junction. Continue 3 miles east to Coleman Pinnacle base, then 0.5 miles to Camp Kiser (~7,000 ft).
firstResearcherNote: Entire list is Heliotrope Ridge and Easton camps; this route approaches over Ptarmigan Ridge, so the Portals camp and Camp Kiser are added. Unsure how often parties descend Coleman-Deming instead.

camps.name: Park Glacier camp near the Portals
camps.notes: Beyond Camp Kiser, across the Rainbow Glacier and onto the Park Glacier. This is where most parties sleep before the Park Glacier Headwall or the Cockscomb.

camps.name: Camp Kiser, Ptarmigan Ridge
camps.notes: About five miles out Ptarmigan Ridge where the maintained trail ends. A good first night, with the glaciers still to cross.

name: Cougar Divide Route
approach: From Glacier, WA, drive Mt. Baker Highway (SR 542) east and turn onto Forest Service Road 33; follow roughly 11 miles of gravel road (rough in sections, high-clearance/SUV recommended, sedans passable with care) to its end at the Cougar Divide Trailhead/parking (room for 8-10 vehicles). Note the true trailhead may be roughly another kilometer past where online mapping apps route. Hike Cougar Divide Trail #601 along the ridge to its high point (~5,920 ft), then continue cross-country northeast along the open ridge, crossing near Dobbs Creek, to Chowder Ridge and the base of Hadley Peak's final …
firstResearcherNote: Cougar Divide is this route's own ridge; Deadhorse basin sits below the way onto Chowder Ridge. Unsure how close the basin is to the Cougar line.

name: Megalodon Ridge
approach: Start at the Rainy Pass trailhead on Highway 20 (large paved lot at ~4,800 ft) and head south on the Pacific Crest Trail. Follow the PCT roughly 9-10 miles, descending along Bridge Creek, to the junction with the North Fork Bridge Creek Trail near North Fork Camp. Continue on this increasingly brushy trail up the North Fork of Bridge Creek valley, crossing Grizzly Creek, to around trail-mile 14, where maintained tread effectively ends and you ford (or find a log crossing of) the North Fork of Bridge Creek - the crossing is easiest a few steps upstream at a cairn. firstResearcherNote: Parties leave the North Fork trail before Grizzly Creek and bivy on a bench below the technical climbing; that bench is added. The Goode Glacier camps serve the Northeast Buttress. Unsure exactly where Walker Park sits relative to the turn-off.

camps.name: Bench bivy below Megalodon Ridge

name: Northeast Face Direct
approach: Mount Formidable is a deep objective on the Ptarmigan Traverse, reached from the same Cascade Pass Trailhead as Mix Up Peak but with a much longer approach. From Cascade Pass, descend to Pelton Basin, cross below Cache Col, and traverse over glaciated and talus terrain past Kool-Aid Lake toward Yang Yang Lakes — typically a full day or more of travel with no maintained trail. From a Yang Yang Lakes camp, climbers make a rising traverse to the notch between Formidable and Spider Mountain, cross the Middle Cascade Glacier, and climb the South Route to the summit. This is a full multi-day mountai…
firstResearcherNote: Rarely climbed; Kool-Aid Lake and the Spider-Formidable Col are the likely bases but the exact approach to the Formidable Glacier face is uncertain.

name: East Ridge (Non-Technical)
approach: From Leavenworth, drive Icicle Road (FR 7601 via Eightmile Road) to the Stuart Lake Trailhead (3,400 ft). Hike the Stuart Lake Trail roughly 2.5 miles (1,100 ft gain) to the Colchuck Lake Trail junction, then switchback up another 1.6 miles (1,100 ft gain) to Colchuck Lake (~4.1 mi, ~2,200 ft total). Continue along the lake's north shore across a boulder field to the base of the Colchuck Glacier.
firstResearcherNote: Assumed to share the Colchuck Glacier approach from the south end of the lake; less certain than the glacier routes.
